questions.stem: Why are complementary sticky ends useful when constructing recombinant DNA?
options: They base-pair and align DNA fragments for ligase
They translate DNA without ribosomes
They destroy every plasmid marker
They prevent all mutation
questions.explanation: Complementary single-stranded overhangs hydrogen-bond, holding the fragments in the correct alignment so DNA ligase can seal the sugar–phosphate backbone.

questions.stem: After bacterial transformation, an antibiotic-resistance gene on the plasmid is used mainly to:
options: Force the insert to replicate outside cells
Identify cells that received the plasmid
Convert the plasmid into a chromosome
Measure the protein's tertiary structure
questions.explanation: Growth on the matching antibiotic selects transformed cells carrying the plasmid. Additional screening may still be needed to confirm that the desired insert is present.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly orders one PCR cycle?
options: Extension → denaturation → translation
Ligation → transcription → annealing
Denaturation → primer annealing → extension
Annealing → meiosis → replication
questions.explanation: Heat separates the DNA strands, cooling allows primers to anneal, and a thermostable polymerase extends from those primers.

questions.stem: Why is an antibody-producing B lymphocyte fused with a myeloma cell during hybridoma production?
options: To remove antibody specificity
To create a bacteriophage
To stop every cell division
To combine specific antibody production with prolonged cell division
questions.explanation: The B cell provides the desired antibody specificity, while the myeloma partner contributes the ability to divide repeatedly in culture.
